title: Showing Team Members How to Perform With Rigor
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses a common leadership blind spot: telling team members to be more rigorous rarely works because most people simply haven't seen rigor demonstrated. The proposed solution is side-by-side modeling — leaders working directly alongside team members on select tasks, narrating the details they attend to and the standards they apply, so that rigor becomes visible rather than abstract. The piece argues this is one of the most consequential applications of leading by example, since precision and thoroughness are hard to teach through instruction alone and are best transmitted by watching a leader apply them in real time.
points: The diagnosis is specific: team members lack rigor not from laziness but because they've literally never observed what rigor looks like in practice.
The prescribed fix is side-by-side modeling on select tasks, not verbal coaching — narrating which details matter and why while doing the work together.
Showcasing rigor is framed as one of the highest-leverage applications of leading by example, more consequential than most other uses of the technique.
quotes: But most fail to be rigorous because they have never seen rigor in action. They don’t know what performance rigor looks like.

The best leaders set the example by engaging side-by-side with team members on select tasks and assignments, showing them along the way how they apply the standards of rigor to the problem or issue at hand.

Good leaders show team members how they go deeper with their analysis, how they achieve more deliberate decision-making, how they find more precision in their execution, and how they become more thoughtful in their advocacy.
The key to teaching rigor is to show team members how to identify the details that matter most and to use them as the foundation for higher performance and greater accuracy.

Leaders who take the time to actively lead by example with team members are usually rewarded with higher quality outcomes and colleagues who have a newfound appreciation for meticulousness in their work.
